Merge Spatial Units into Larger Regions

Source: R/map-tools.R
combineRegions.Rd

Unions the geometries of a map by a grouping, e.g. municipalities to premium regions or cantons to language areas. Use it to map any regional division that is defined as a set of municipalities or cantons.

Usage

combineRegions(map, groups, id = NULL)

Arguments

map

an sf object, e.g. from geoGemeinde() or geoKanton().

groups

grouping, along the rows of map or, if id is given, along id; units with NA are left out.

id

optional ids of the units groups refers to, cantons also by abbreviation. An id may occur repeatedly only with the same group (such duplicates are dropped); an id assigned to different groups is an error, as a unit cannot be part of two regions. Resolve such units explicitly before, e.g. the municipalities split over several premium regions (split_l in praemienregion()).

Value

An sf object with one row per group: the column groups (sorted) and the unioned geometry.

Note

Based on code by Juerg Guggenbuehl, adapted to conform to package standards.

See also

praemienregion(), raumgliederung().

Other swiss.spatial: geocode(), locate(), neighbours()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
preg <- praemienregion(2023)
geo  <- geoGemeinde(as.Date("2023-01-01"))
# municipalities split over several regions: own group "mehrere"
preg$preg_x[preg$split_l] <- "mehrere"
reg  <- combineRegions(geo, preg$preg_x, id = preg$gem_id)
plotMap(reg)
} # }
